title: Incomplete in degree, complete in essential parts
source_text: XXVI. Caeterum quum justitiam quae fidelibus inest inchoatam nominant, per id negare nolunt illam completam esse quoad essentiam & partes integrantes. Et similiter, quum imperfectam affirmant, per id non significant aliquid ei deesse, quod necessario pertineat ad veram rationem justitiae & sanctitatis. Imo enim illi concedunt perfectio-nem partium essentialium atque integrantium. Nec putant illam esse justitiam & san-ctitatem, vel mancam & mutilam, vel apparentem & falso sic dictam; sed veram & synceram, suis omnibus membris & partibus constantem: utpote per quam homo toti legi divinae, licet non exacte, conformis reddatur, & quae proinde justitiae & sanctitatis verae totam & integram rationem habeat. Unde est quod in hoc negotio saepe distinguunt inter perfectionem graduum, & perfectionem partium, sive essentia-lium, sive integrantium. Ac priorem eam illi inhaerenti nostrae justitiae convenire pernegant, sed posteriorem illi non deesse fatentur & asserunt.
pass_a_gloss: But when they call the righteousness that is in believers begun, they do not thereby wish to deny that it is complete as to essence and integrating parts. And likewise, when they affirm it imperfect, they do not thereby signify that something is lacking to it which necessarily belongs to the true nature of righteousness and holiness. For they grant the perfection of essential and integrating parts. Nor do they think that righteousness and holiness to be maimed and mutilated, or apparent and falsely so called, but true and sincere, consisting of all its members and parts: inasmuch as by it man is rendered conformable to the whole divine law, though not exactly, and therefore has the whole and entire nature of true righteousness and holiness. Hence in this matter they often distinguish between perfection of degrees and perfection of parts, whether essential or integrating. And they utterly deny that the former belongs to our inherent righteousness, but confess and assert that the latter is not lacking to it.
pass_b_english: Inchoate does not deny completeness of essence and integrating parts; imperfect does not mean lacking what belongs to true justice.
They distinguish perfection of degrees (denied here) from perfection of essential/integrating parts (affirmed).

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1060.
